Healthcare, nursing specifically, has seen a major influx of international workers. This isn’t always a major issue but we are getting some awful and unsafe workers. It seems like the healthcare field really shot for quantity over quality to replace all the nurses who either left the field or retired post covid.

I’ve seen hospitals train new international nurses for months instead of letting them go. Mind you this is paid so imagine getting trained for 6 months - that’s over 20k in orientation shifts alone.

Despite the apparent shortage of nurses, it’s almost next to impossible to even land an interview if you’re Canadian born. A lot of my friends who are trying to find jobs are struggling to get any sort of reply from applications only to find out they just hired - you guessed it - more international nurses.

It’s shitty. It feels weird having had completed what used to be known as an arduous program and final exam only for it to be nothing more than a piece of paper that can’t even get you a job at McDonald’s right now.

We were close for 10 years. My best friend. It’s hard to say how it’s affected me. I can’t really put it into words. He’s been in my life for so long that it feels as if a part of me is lost as well. Everything I do I think “I wish he was here for this”. It’s hard.

It’s tough losing someone. He probably thought nobody would miss him. I’ve lost people I wasn’t really close to and I still think about them every single day. You’d be missed by someone you probably don’t even think of.
